subject: MAP: unit-cost stress playbook — prefetch & batching acceptance
messages:
From: Ethan Ross <ethan@medexa.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2024-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — token/unit economics clarifications

David / Laura,

Thanks for the MAP draft this morning. We reviewed the financial gating items and have a couple of critical asks before we sign off on the pilot timeline:

- Can you confirm the tokens-per-user assumptions for the chat flow (session length ~ 3 turns, avg 600 tokens in/out)?
- How does Redwood model the impact of prefix caching vs. per-request KV cache hits — we need both a conservative and optimistic tokens/$ view for procurement.
- Are there hard SLOs where batching (to reduce unit cost) would jeopardize the <250ms p95 latency target for our interactive flows?

Procurement also requested any spreadsheets you have with scenario runs (tokens/$ at different cache/hit rates) so they can preview budget impact.

Appreciate a quick reply — our internal legal wants the MAP locked by EOD Monday if numbers are stable.

Best,
Ethan Ross
Head of Product, Medexa

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan@medexa.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2024-07-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — token/unit economics clarifications

Ethan — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a quick modeling workbook and a small prefetch sim (see attachments). High level answers below; Ben and Karthik are looped for technical detail and acceptance gates.

Quick answers:
1) Tokens per session: our base-case for MAP assumes 3.2 model turns /session (user + assistant pairs) and 650 avg tokens in/out (includes instruction overhead). That maps to ~2,080 tokens/session. We also include a 15% headroom for longer threads.

2) Caching: prefix and KV cache are treated orthogonally in the model. The spreadsheet has three columns for cache hit-rate scenarios:
   - Conservative: 5% prefix hit, 0% KV reuse (cold start heavy)
   - Expected: 25% prefix hit, 40% KV reuse (typical form-fill + few repeated prompts)
   - Aggressive: 50% prefix hit, 70% KV reuse (high repeatability / templated flows)
Tokens/$ shown per 10M tokens, plus equivalent cost per 1k DAU at average session length.

3) Batching vs latency: default Redwood batching (continuous batching with a 10ms hold) can reduce per-token compute by ~12–18% for these model sizes without adding >15ms median latency. However, to maintain p95 <250ms we recommend constraining batching window and enabling adaptive priority routing. The workbook includes a latency tradeoff sheet with simulated p50/p95 for different batch sizes and traffic shapes.

Action items from our side:
- Ben: drop a short note on how the prefetch sim was constructed and where to read the KV reuse numbers.
- Karthik: propose explicit MAP acceptance criteria (tokens/$ thresholds at 3 cache scenarios + max allowed p95 impact).

Ethan — we can get a finalized MAP appendix with the numbers by COB Monday if the procurement team can accept the conservative scenario as a start.

Cheers,
David Kim
Head of FinOps, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: token_modeling_spreadsheet.xlsx (workbook: scenario tabs + assumptions), prefetch-sim.csv (sample traffic sim)

Date: 2024-07-19T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — token/unit economics clarifications

Quick technical note on the sim and assumptions so procurement has context:

- Prefetch sim: we replayed a sampled subset of your anonymized request traces (thank you) and injected a 10% templating signal to estimate prefix hit rates. The sim outputs are in prefetch-sim.csv.
- KV reuse: measured as a percent of requests that reuse cached KV entries without recomputing first-token layers. This is traffic-dependent; our expected column assumes form-based flows where users iterate on a small set of prompts.
- Cost deltas: for the LLM family you're evaluating, moving from no caching to expected-caching reduces GPU token compute by ~22% (including memory transfer savings). Quantization to int8 adds another 6% savings on typical encoder-decoder variants.

Important caveats:
- Prefetching increases memory pressure and warm-up cost; we amortize that over expected session counts in the workbook.
- Batching gains are nonlinear for bursts — if you have spiky traffic we recommend the conservative gating thresholds in the spreadsheet (see tab: "MAP Gates").

If you want, we can extract a short one-pager that procurement can sign (numbers + acceptance criteria) and leave the full workbook as an appendix.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan@medexa.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2024-07-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — token/unit economics clarifications

Ethan — following up with proposed MAP acceptance criteria (technical & finance) that we recommend adding to the mutual action plan. Please review and flag anything you can't accept.

Proposed MAP acceptance criteria (add to MAP appendix):
1) Tokens/$ thresholds (per 1M tokens):
   - Conservative gate: <= $12.50 / 1M tokens (assumes 5% prefix, 0% KV reuse, no quantization)
   - Baseline gate: <= $9.75 / 1M tokens (assumes 25% prefix, 40% KV reuse, int8 quantization available)
   - Aggressive gate: <= $7.80 / 1M tokens (50% prefix, 70% KV reuse, int8 + kernel optimizations)

2) Latency impact:
   - p95 user-facing latency increase vs baseline must be <= 30ms when enabling batching/prefetch in the baseline gate. If p95 increase >30ms, we revert to the conservative gate until optimizations are in place.

3) Eval plan & regressions:
   - Before enabling aggressive caching, Medexa will run the Redwood eval harness on a 500-case prompt set (we can supply) and must not exceed 3% semantic drift vs baseline for critical intents.
   - Any quality regression >3% triggers rollback and a joint debug period (max 72 hours).

4) Rollout / rollback playbook:
   - Canary at 5% traffic for 6 hours, monitor tokens/$, p95, and quality metrics. If gates pass, ramp to 25% for 12 hours, then full rollout.

If those sound OK, David — can you incorporate the numbers in the MAP appendix and send the one-pager for procurement sign-off? If procurement needs the conservative numbers locked in contractually we can do that and make the baseline gate an operational target.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Product — Inference, Redwood Inference
